metadata.design_principle: Flat (dataset, language) rows — deduplicated across benchmarks.

benchmarks.name: AfroBench
benchmarks.description: AfroBench is a comprehensive multi-task benchmark for evaluating LLM performance across 64 African languages, comprising 15 NLP tasks and 22 datasets spanning NLU, text generation, QA, and reasoning. It aggregates existing African language evaluation datasets and introduces one new dataset (AfriADR) for diacritics restoration.

citation.paper_title: AfroBench: A Comprehensive Multilingual Benchmark for African Languages

benchmarks.name: Aya_Evaluation_Suite
benchmarks.description: A multilingual evaluation suite for assessing open-ended generation quality of LLMs, consisting of 25,750 prompts: 250 original human-curated prompts in each of 7 languages, 200 machine-translated prompts from English Dolly in 101 languages (114 dialects), and human post-edited translations of those prompts in 6 languages.

citation.paper_title: Aya Evaluation Suite

benchmarks.name: BHASA
benchmarks.description: BHASA is a holistic linguistic and cultural evaluation suite for LLMs in Southeast Asian languages, comprising an NLP benchmark (8 tasks across NLU, NLG, NLR), LINDSEA (a handcrafted linguistic diagnostic toolkit covering syntax, semantics, and pragmatics), and cultural diagnostics (cultural representation and sensitivity). It currently covers Indonesian, Vietnamese, Thai, and Tamil for the NLP benchmark, and Indonesian and Tamil for LINDSEA and cultural diagnostics.

citation.paper_title: BHASA: A Holistic Southeast Asian Linguistic and Cultural Evaluation Suite

benchmarks.name: BUFFET
benchmarks.description: BUFFET (Benchmark of Unified Format Few-shot Transfer Evaluation) is a benchmark for few-shot cross-lingual transfer that unifies 15 diverse NLP tasks across 54 typologically diverse languages in a sequence-to-sequence format, providing fixed few-shot examples and instructions for rigorous comparisons of multilingual language models using both fine-tuning and in-context learning.

citation.paper_title: BUFFET: Benchmarking Large Language Models for Few-shot Cross-lingual Transfer

benchmarks.name: BeMyCheese
benchmarks.description: A large-scale human evaluation benchmark for assessing cultural localisation in machine translation by multilingual LLMs. Evaluates 7 LLMs across 15 target languages with 5 native-speaker raters per language on both full-text translations and segment-level culturally nuanced language (idioms, puns, holidays, cultural concepts) on a 0-3 ordinal quality scale.

citation.paper_title: BeMyCheese: A Large-Scale Human Evaluation Benchmark for Multilingual LLMs

benchmarks.name: Belebele
benchmarks.description: A fully parallel multiple-choice machine reading comprehension (MRC) benchmark spanning 122 language variants across 29 scripts and 27 language families, with 900 questions based on passages from the FLORES-200 dataset. Questions were created in English and professionally translated to all target languages.

citation.paper_title: The Belebele Benchmark: a Parallel Reading Comprehension Dataset in 122 Language Variants

benchmarks.name: BenchMAX
benchmarks.description: BenchMAX is a comprehensive multilingual evaluation suite covering 10 diverse tasks across 6 capabilities (instruction following, code generation, reasoning, long context understanding, tool use, and translation) in 17 languages. Data is machine-translated from English and post-edited by three native annotators per sample to ensure quality.

citation.paper_title: BenchMAX: A Multilingual Benchmark for Evaluating LLMs Across Languages

benchmarks.name: BhashaBench_V1
benchmarks.description: BhashaBench V1 is a domain-specific, multi-task, bilingual (English and Hindi) benchmark containing 74,166 question-answer pairs across four India-centric domains: Agriculture, Legal, Finance, and Ayurveda. Questions are sourced from authentic government and professional examination papers, spanning 90+ subdomains and 500+ topics.

citation.paper_title: BhashaBench V1

benchmarks.name: BoolQ
benchmarks.description: BoolQ is a reading comprehension dataset of 16,000 naturally occurring yes/no questions paired with Wikipedia passages. Questions are gathered from anonymized Google search queries and annotated by humans following the Natural Questions pipeline.

citation.paper_title: BoolQ: Exploring the Surprising Difficulty of Natural Yes/No Questions

benchmarks.name: CL-IFEval
benchmarks.description: CL-IFEval and CL-GSM Symbolic are cross-lingual functional evaluation benchmarks created by translating English IFEval (541 prompts) and GSM-Symbolic (100 templates) into French, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, and Yoruba via Google Translate with native-speaker validation, designed to measure functional multilingual performance and robustness of LLMs beyond static data benchmarks.

citation.paper_title: Multi-lingual Functional Evaluation for Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: CulturalBench
benchmarks.description: CulturalBench is an English-only benchmark of 1,696 human-written and human-verified multiple-choice questions assessing LMs' cultural knowledge across 45 global regions and 17 cultural topics. It includes two evaluation setups: CulturalBench-Easy (multiple-choice) and CulturalBench-Hard (True/False binary for each option, yielding 6,784 questions).

citation.paper_title: CulturalBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Cultural Knowledge of LLMs

benchmarks.name: FLORES-101
benchmarks.description: A high-quality evaluation benchmark for multilingual machine translation consisting of 3001 English Wikipedia sentences professionally translated into 101 languages, enabling many-to-many evaluation of 10,100 translation directions.

citation.paper_title: The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation

benchmarks.name: FluidQA
benchmarks.description: FLUID QA is the first multilingual benchmark evaluating figurative language usage in dialogue across English, Korean, and Chinese, covering four rhetorical categories (idiom, metaphor, simile, sarcasm). It is accompanied by FLUTE-bi, a sentence-level binary classification diagnostic task for figurative recognition.

citation.paper_title: FluidQA: Question Answering for Fluid Intelligence

benchmarks.name: GSM8K
benchmarks.description: GSM8K is a dataset of 8.5K high-quality grade school math word problems in English with natural language solutions, requiring 2-8 step reasoning using basic arithmetic operations. It was designed to diagnose multi-step mathematical reasoning failures in large language models.

citation.paper_title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems

benchmarks.name: INDIC-DIALECT
benchmarks.description: A human-curated parallel corpus of 13,000 sentence pairs spanning 11 Indian dialects and 2 standard languages (Hindi and Odia) from three Indian states (Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Odisha), used to construct a multi-task benchmark evaluating dialect classification, multiple-choice question answering, and machine translation between dialects and their corresponding standard languages.

citation.paper_title: INDIC-DIALECT: Multilingual Dialectal Benchmark for Indian Languages

benchmarks.name: IberoBench
benchmarks.description: IberoBench is a multilingual, multi-task benchmark for evaluating LLMs in five Iberian languages (Catalan, European Spanish, Basque, Galician, and European Portuguese), consisting of 62 tasks divided into 179 subtasks across 10 categories, built on the LM Evaluation Harness framework. It combines 40 existing high-quality datasets with 22 newly created or translated datasets, emphasizing quality, reproducibility, and cultural adaptation.

citation.paper_title: IberoBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating NLP in Iberian Languages

benchmarks.name: IndiSentiment140
benchmarks.description: IndiSentiment140 is a sentiment analysis dataset for 22 Indian languages created by machine-translating the English Sentiment140 Twitter corpus (1.6M tweets) into each language using Google Translate, preserving the original binary sentiment labels (positive/negative).

citation.paper_title: IndiSentiment140

benchmarks.name: IndicIFEval
benchmarks.description: IndicIFEval is a benchmark for evaluating verifiable instruction-following in 14 Indic languages, comprising two subsets: IndicIFEval-Trans (translated and localized from English IFEval) and IndicIFEval-Ground (synthetically generated instructions grounded in native Indic content from the Sangraha corpus), with ~800 human-verified examples per language.

citation.paper_title: IndicIFEval: A Benchmark for Verifiable Instruction-Following in Indic Languages

benchmarks.name: IndicMMLU-Pro
benchmarks.description: IndicMMLU-Pro is a machine-translated adaptation of the English MMLU-Pro benchmark into 9 Indic languages (Hindi, Bengali, Telugu, Marathi, Tamil, Gujarati, Urdu, Kannada, Punjabi), covering 14 subject categories for evaluating LLM multi-task language understanding. Translation was performed using IndicTrans2 and validated via back-translation metrics and expert proofreading by 13 native-speaker reviewers.

citation.paper_title: IndicMMLU-Pro

benchmarks.name: IndicNLG
benchmarks.description: IndicNLG Benchmark is a collection of datasets for benchmarking NLG performance across 5 diverse tasks (biography generation, headline generation, sentence summarization, paraphrase generation, question generation) spanning 11 Indic languages, comprising approximately 8.5M examples total. It is the first NLG benchmark for Indic languages.

citation.paper_title: IndicNLG Suite: Multilingual Datasets for Diverse NLG Tasks in Indic Languages

benchmarks.name: IndicNLPSuite
benchmarks.description: IndicNLPSuite provides monolingual corpora (IndicCorp), pre-trained word embeddings (IndicFT), language models (IndicBERT), and an NLU evaluation benchmark (IndicGLUE) for 11 major Indian languages from the Indo-Aryan and Dravidian families, comprising newly created semi-automatic datasets and curated existing datasets across tasks including text classification, QA, NER, NLI, paraphrase detection, and sentiment analysis.

citation.paper_title: IndicNLPSuite: Monolingual Corpora, Evaluation Benchmarks and Pre-trained Multilingual Language Models for Indian Languages

benchmarks.name: IndicParam
benchmarks.description: A human-curated benchmark of over 13,000 multiple-choice questions covering 11 low- and extremely low-resource Indic languages, sourced from UGC-NET graduate-level examinations administered by the Government of India. Questions are classified as language understanding or general knowledge, and annotated with six question types (MCQ, assertion & reason, list matching, fill in the blanks, identify incorrect statement, ordering).

citation.paper_title: IndicParam: Benchmark to Evaluate LLMs on Low-resource Indic Languages

benchmarks.name: IndicXTREME
benchmarks.description: IndicXTREME is a human-supervised NLU benchmark for Indic languages consisting of nine diverse tasks (five classification, two structure prediction, one QA, one retrieval) covering 20 languages from 4 language families, with 105 evaluation sets of which 52 are new contributions. It is designed to test zero-shot cross-lingual transfer of pretrained language models.

citation.paper_title: IndicXTREME: A Multi-Task Benchmark For Evaluating Indic Languages

benchmarks.name: IrokoBench
benchmarks.description: IrokoBench is a human-translated benchmark for 17 typologically-diverse low-resource African languages, comprising three tasks: natural language inference (AfriXNLI, from XNLI), multi-choice knowledge QA (AfriMMLU, from MMLU), and mathematical reasoning (AfriMGSM, from MGSM). It evaluates LLMs on complex reasoning and knowledge-intensive tasks for African languages.

citation.paper_title: IrokoBench: A New Benchmark for African Languages in the Age of Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: JailNewsBench
benchmarks.description: JailNewsBench is the first benchmark for evaluating LLM robustness against jailbreak-induced fake news generation, spanning 34 regions and 22 languages with approximately 300k instances, 8 evaluation sub-metrics through LLM-as-a-Judge, and 5 jailbreak attack methods.

citation.paper_title: JailNewsBench: A Multilingual Jailbreak and News Safety Benchmark

benchmarks.name: LinguaSafe
benchmarks.description: A comprehensive multilingual safety benchmark for LLMs comprising 45k entries across 12 languages (high-, medium-, and low-resource), curated using a combination of translated, transcreated, and natively-sourced data. Features a hierarchical safety taxonomy with 5 domains and 23 subtypes, severity-level annotations (L0-L3), and both direct (MCQ) and indirect evaluation frameworks including oversensitivity assessment.

citation.paper_title: LinguaSafe: A Comprehensive Multilingual Safety Benchmark for Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: M-IFEval
benchmarks.description: M-IFEval is a multilingual extension of the IFEval benchmark that evaluates LLM instruction-following abilities in French, Japanese, and Spanish (plus English from the original IFEval), using both shared and language-specific verifiable instructions covering formatting, punctuation, script-based, and special-character constraints.

citation.paper_title: M-IFEval: Multilingual Instruction Following Evaluation

benchmarks.name: M3Exam
benchmarks.description: M3Exam is a benchmark of 12,317 multiple-choice questions sourced from real official human exams in 9 languages across 3 educational levels (primary, middle, high school), covering 4 subject categories (language, math, social science, natural science), with approximately 23% of questions requiring image processing.

citation.paper_title: M3Exam: A Multilingual, Multimodal, Multilevel Benchmark for Examining Large Language Models

benchmarks.name: MAKIEVAL
benchmarks.description: MAKIEVAL is an automatic multilingual framework for evaluating cultural awareness in LLMs through open-ended text generation, leveraging Wikidata as a cross-lingual anchor to extract and link cultural entities without translation. It evaluates 7 LLMs across 13 languages, 19 countries/regions, and 6 culturally salient topics using four metrics: granularity, diversity, culture specificity, and culture consensus.

citation.paper_title: MAKIEVAL: A Multilingual Automatic WikiData-based Framework for Evaluation

benchmarks.name: MATH
benchmarks.description: MATH is a dataset of 12,500 challenging competition mathematics problems (from AMC 10, AMC 12, AIME, etc.) with step-by-step solutions in LaTeX, spanning 7 subjects and 5 difficulty levels. It is accompanied by AMPS, a large auxiliary pretraining corpus of over 5 million mathematics problems from Khan Academy and Mathematica scripts.

citation.paper_title: Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset

benchmarks.name: MEGA
benchmarks.description: MEGA (Multilingual Evaluation of Generative AI) is the first large-scale benchmarking of generative LLMs across multilingual settings, evaluating GPT-3.5, GPT-4, and BLOOMZ on 16 existing NLP datasets spanning 70 typologically diverse languages covering 21 language families, with analysis of prompting strategies, performance disparities across languages, and test data contamination.

citation.paper_title: MEGA: Multilingual Evaluation of Generative AI

benchmarks.name: MILU
benchmarks.description: MILU (Multi-task Indic Language Understanding Benchmark) is a comprehensive evaluation benchmark covering 8 domains and 41 subjects across 11 Indic languages (including English), with ~79,617 multiple-choice questions sourced from Indian national, state, and regional competitive examinations. It emphasizes India-centric, culturally relevant knowledge alongside standard academic subjects.

citation.paper_title: MILU: A Multi-task Indic Language Understanding Benchmark

benchmarks.name: MMLU-ProX
benchmarks.description: MMLU-ProX is a multilingual benchmark extending MMLU-Pro to 29 typologically diverse languages, containing 11,829 parallel multiple-choice questions (10 options) per language across 57 subjects and 14 disciplines. It uses a semi-automated LLM translation pipeline with expert verification to enable direct cross-linguistic comparison of LLM reasoning capabilities.

citation.paper_title: MMLU-ProX: Multilingual MMLU-Pro

benchmarks.name: MMTEB
benchmarks.description: MMTEB (Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark) is a large-scale, community-driven expansion of MTEB, covering over 500 quality-controlled evaluation tasks across 10 task categories and 1051 languages (250+ excluding bitext mining), spanning diverse domains including fiction, social media, medical texts, and programming documentation. It constructs several sub-benchmarks including MTEB(Multilingual) with 132 tasks, MTEB(Europe) with 74 tasks, MTEB(Indic) with 23 tasks, and MTEB(eng, v2) with 41 tasks.

citation.paper_title: MMTEB: Massive Multilingual Text Embedding Benchmark

benchmarks.name: MUCH
benchmarks.description: MUCH is a multilingual claim-level hallucination benchmark comprising 4,873 LLM-generated responses (20,751 claims) across four European languages (English, French, Spanish, German), with binary factuality annotations and 24 logits per token, designed for evaluating uncertainty quantification methods under realistic deployment conditions.

citation.paper_title: MUCH: Multilingual Understanding and Cultural Handling Benchmark

benchmarks.name: MUG_Eval
benchmarks.description: MUG-Eval is a language-agnostic proxy evaluation framework that assesses LLMs' multilingual generation capabilities by transforming existing benchmarks into conversational information-gap tasks, using task success rate as a proxy for generation quality. It evaluates 8 LLMs across 30 languages (high/mid/low-resource) on three tasks without requiring language-specific NLP tools, human annotations, or LLM-as-judge, and claims scalability to 2,102 languages via GlotLID.

citation.paper_title: MUG_Eval: Multilingual Generation Evaluation

benchmarks.name: MaXIFE
benchmarks.description: MaXIFE is a multilingual and cross-lingual instruction-following evaluation benchmark covering 23 languages with 1667 verifiable instruction tasks across 47 instruction subcategories, combining rule-based and model-based evaluation strategies.

citation.paper_title: MaXIFE: Massively Multilingual Instruction-Following Evaluation

benchmarks.name: MultiJail
benchmarks.description: A multilingual jailbreak dataset comprising 3150 samples across 10 languages (English plus 9 non-English), designed to evaluate LLM safety under two scenarios: unintentional (non-English users inadvertently bypassing safety) and intentional (malicious users combining multilingual prompts with jailbreak instructions).

citation.paper_title: MultiJail: A Multilingual Jailbreak Benchmark

benchmarks.name: Naamapadam
benchmarks.description: Naamapadam is the largest publicly available NER dataset for 11 major Indian languages from two language families (Indo-Aryan and Dravidian), containing 5.7M sentences and 9.4M entities across three categories (Person, Location, Organization). Training data is automatically created via annotation projection from English using parallel corpora, while manually annotated test sets are provided for 9 languages.

citation.paper_title: Naamapadam: A Large-Scale Named Entity Recognition Dataset for Indian Languages

benchmarks.name: PTP
benchmarks.description: A large-scale multilingual benchmark of 425K naturally occurring prompts across 17 languages for evaluating neural toxic degeneration in LLMs, created by scraping over 100M web-text documents from mC4 and The Pile corpora and scoring them with Perspective API. PTPSmall is a stratified 5K-per-language subset for lower-cost benchmarking.

citation.paper_title: PTP: Parallel Translation Probing

benchmarks.name: SeaHELM
benchmarks.description: SEA-HELM (SouthEast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models) is a holistic multilingual and multicultural LLM evaluation suite for Southeast Asian languages, comprising five core pillars: NLP Classics, LLM-Specifics, SEA Linguistics, SEA Culture, and Safety. It currently supports Filipino, Indonesian, Tamil, Thai, and Vietnamese, combining collated native-language and translated datasets with newly created benchmarks (SEA-IFEval, SEA-MTBench, LINDSEA).

citation.paper_title: SeaHELM: A Holistic Evaluation of Southeast Asian Languages in LLMs

benchmarks.name: TUMLU
benchmarks.description: A comprehensive, natively developed multilingual language understanding benchmark for Turkic languages, consisting of 38,139 middle- and high-school level multiple-choice questions across 11 academic subjects in 9 Turkic languages (Azerbaijani, Crimean Tatar, Karakalpak, Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, Turkish, Uyghur, and Uzbek). TUMLU-mini is a balanced and manually verified subset with ~100 questions per subject per language.

citation.paper_title: TUMLU: Turkish Multilingual Understanding Benchmark

benchmarks.name: TriviaQA
benchmarks.description: TriviaQA is a large-scale reading comprehension dataset containing over 650K question-answer-evidence triples, with 95K question-answer pairs authored by trivia enthusiasts and independently gathered evidence documents from Wikipedia and the Web. It tests complex compositional questions, lexical/syntactic variability, and multi-sentence reasoning.

citation.paper_title: TriviaQA: A Large Scale Distantly Supervised Challenge Dataset for Reading Comprehension

benchmarks.name: Uhuru
benchmarks.description: Uhura is a benchmark for evaluating scientific question answering and truthfulness in six low-resource African languages (Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili, Yoruba, Zulu), created via professional human translation of ARC-Easy and TruthfulQA from English.

citation.paper_title: Uhuru: A Benchmark for Evaluating Scientific Question Answering

benchmarks.name: XGLUE
benchmarks.description: XGLUE is a cross-lingual benchmark covering 11 tasks (both understanding and generation) across 19 languages, with English-only training data for each task. It includes 5 existing multilingual datasets and 6 new tasks from Search, Ads, and News scenarios.

citation.paper_title: XGLUE: A New Benchmark Dataset for Cross-lingual Pre-training, Understanding and Generation

benchmarks.name: XNLI
benchmarks.description: XNLI is a cross-lingual natural language inference evaluation corpus consisting of 7500 human-annotated development and test examples translated from English MultiNLI data into 14 other languages (15 total), covering three-way NLI classification (entailment, contradiction, neutral).

citation.paper_title: XNLI: Evaluating Cross-lingual Sentence Representations

benchmarks.name: XORQA
benchmarks.description: XOR QA is a cross-lingual open-retrieval question answering benchmark built on 40K information-seeking questions across 7 typologically diverse non-English languages (inherited from TyDi QA's unanswerable questions). It defines three tasks of increasing complexity: XOR-Retrieve (cross-lingual paragraph retrieval), XOR-EnglishSpan (L-to-English open-retrieval QA), and XOR-Full (round-trip answer generation in the target language).

citation.paper_title: XOR QA: Cross-lingual Open-Retrieval Question Answering

benchmarks.name: XQuAD
benchmarks.description: XQuAD is a cross-lingual extractive question answering benchmark consisting of 240 paragraphs and 1190 question-answer pairs from the SQuAD v1.1 development set, professionally translated from English into 10 languages (Spanish, German, Greek, Russian, Turkish, Arabic, Vietnamese, Thai, Chinese, Hindi).

citation.paper_title: On the Cross-lingual Transferability of Monolingual Representations

benchmarks.name: XTREME
benchmarks.description: XTREME (Cross-lingual TRansfer Evaluation of Multilingual Encoders) is a multi-task benchmark for evaluating the cross-lingual generalization capabilities of multilingual representations. It covers 40 typologically diverse languages spanning 12 language families and includes 9 tasks across classification, structured prediction, question answering, and sentence retrieval.

citation.paper_title: XTREME: A Massively Multilingual Multi-task Benchmark for Evaluating Cross-lingual Generalisation

benchmarks.name: XTREME-R
benchmarks.description: XTREME-R (XTREME Revisited) is a multilingual benchmark consisting of 10 natural language understanding tasks covering 50 typologically diverse languages, extending XTREME with more challenging tasks including language-agnostic retrieval, a multilingual diagnostic suite (MultiCheckList), and fine-grained evaluation capabilities via an interactive leaderboard.

citation.paper_title: XTREME-R: Towards More Challenging and Nuanced Multilingual Evaluation

benchmarks.name: XTREME_UP
benchmarks.description: XTREME-UP is a multilingual benchmark focusing on user-centric tasks in a scarce-data setting for 88 under-represented languages across 9 key technologies including ASR, OCR, MT, and information access tasks. It standardizes multilingual in-language fine-tuning based on realistic annotation costs (8 hours per language).

citation.paper_title: XTREME-UP: A User-Centric Scarce-Data Benchmark for Under-Represented Languages
